confidence.reason: Rate-limiter ownership and reset behavior are explicit in source; multi-replica request distribution was not executed in this source-only run.

description: Request throttling uses a process-local in-memory RateLimiter registry owned by each application process. In a multi-replica hosted deployment, each replica enforces the same nominal per-IP bucket independently, so aggregate traffic across replicas can exceed the intended shared limit.

evidence.description: Registry is explicitly per caller/process and isolated between app instances in the same process.
main.py owns one process-wide registry; no shared/distributed throttle state.
Throttling is explicitly hosted-only and relies on this registry.
Supported deployment discussions contemplate web replicas/workers sharing load while throttle state remains local.

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated remote client able to distribute requests across web replicas.
instructions: Deploy hosted mode with more than one web replica behind the proxy.
Send login/callback/sync/cache-clear requests at the nominal per-IP limit toward each replica identity.
Observe that each replica accepts up to its local bucket, so aggregate accepted requests exceed the nominal shared bucket.
Confirm that no shared throttle store coordinates the replicas.
execution.observed_result: Aggregate accepted abusive requests scale with replica count because each replica maintains an independent token bucket.
payloads: Repeated POST /api/auth/login/start, GET /api/auth/callback failures, POST /api/sync, DELETE /api/cache and DELETE /api/me/cache at the nominal per-IP limit per replica

intended_behavior: Abuse throttling for internet-facing authentication, sync, and destructive endpoints should enforce the intended shared limit regardless of how many web replicas accept traffic.

code_changes.fixed_code: Replace the process-local RateLimiter for internet-facing buckets with shared throttle state, or document the deployment as single-web-replica-only and enforce that topology in compose/deployment checks.

remediation.strategy: Use shared rate-limit state for externally reachable buckets when multiple web replicas are supported; otherwise constrain the supported topology to one web replica and check it at deployment time.

root_cause: Process-local in-memory rate-limit buckets with no shared coordination across web replicas.

impact.reason: Abuse controls weaken as replicas scale; this permits more abusive throughput but does not itself bypass authentication or expose another tenant.

likelihood.reason: Requires a multi-replica deployment and distributed abusive traffic; single-replica deployments and Cloudflare edge controls reduce exposure.

confidence.reason: Source trace is complete and the missing timeout is visible on every failure and success path; socket-hang duration was not measured because target execution was unavailable.

description: The hosted Turnstile verification path performs an outbound HTTPS POST to Cloudflare siteverify without a socket timeout. The vulnerable call is reachable from an unauthenticated endpoint, POST /api/auth/login/start, before any authenticated session is required.

evidence.description: httplib2.Http() is constructed with no timeout argument, unlike TOKEN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS used for Google token calls.
The no-timeout response is used as the sole pass/fail gate for login initiation.
Callers propagate the unbounded result without adding their own time bound.
Google token exchange in the same codebase uses an explicit 30-second timeout, establishing that unbounded outbound calls are not the intended pattern.

instructions: Configure hosted mode with Turnstile enabled.
POST /api/auth/login/start with an attacker-chosen token while Cloudflare siteverify is slow or unresponsive.
Observe that the affected request thread remains occupied for the duration of the outbound socket wait.
Repeat with a small number of concurrent unauthenticated requests and observe shared request-handling capacity being retained.
execution.observed_result: Each affected login-start request retains its worker while waiting on siteverify; sustained slow responses retain shared request-handling capacity.

intended_behavior: Unauthenticated outbound verification calls should have an explicit low timeout and fail closed, so a slow verification provider cannot retain shared request-handling capacity.

remediation.strategy: Add an explicit low timeout to the Turnstile siteverify POST and keep fail-closed behavior; use the same bounded-transport pattern already used by oauth_transport.

root_cause: Missing outbound timeout on the Cloudflare Turnstile siteverify POST in _verify_turnstile.

impact.reason: Shared request-handling capacity can be retained by slow verification responses; no credential, tenant-data, or code-execution boundary is crossed.

likelihood.reason: The affected endpoint is unauthenticated and the timeout is absent on every call, but exploitation needs sustained slow siteverify responses and competes with existing per-IP login throttling.

title: Turnstile siteverify POST has no outbound timeout

description: The compose deployment pins postgres and Caddy images but tracks cloudflared through the mutable cloudflare/cloudflared:latest tag. A rebuild or redeploy can therefore silently change the edge tunnel binary without a source change or review.

evidence.description: cloudflared service uses the mutable latest tag while warning that pinning matters.
Same file pins postgres to postgres:16-alpine.
Same file pins Caddy to caddy:2-alpine.
Runtime backend image pins exact dependency versions for reproducible deploys.

execution.attacker_perspective: Operator/supply-chain observer reviewing reproducible deployment inputs.
instructions: Inspect compose.yml image references for the edge tunnel versus postgres and Caddy.
Rebuild or redeploy at two different times and record the resolved cloudflared digest.
Observe that the tunnel image can change without any repository change.
Confirm that no digest pin or update-review step constrains the edge binary.
execution.observed_result: The tunnel image reference is mutable: redeploys can silently change edge software while the repository remains unchanged.

intended_behavior: Public-edge deployment inputs should be pinned and reviewable so rebuilds do not silently change tunnel software.

code_changes.fixed_code: image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.1  # replace with the reviewed/tested release and update deliberately, or pin by digest.

remediation.strategy: Pin cloudflared to a tested version or digest and update it through deliberate dependency changes, matching the treatment of postgres and Caddy.

root_cause: Mutable latest image tag for the Cloudflare Tunnel edge container.

impact.reason: Edge software can change silently; no direct credential disclosure or tenant compromise is demonstrated by the tag alone.

likelihood.reason: Requires an upstream image change coinciding with redeploy; routine rebuilds make this plausible over time.
